sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Create an environment, start a project and launch the development server:

snippets.code:
# Create and activate a virtual environment
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install Django
pip install "django>=5.1,<5.3"

# Start a project in the current directory
django-admin startproject config .

# Create an application
python manage.py startapp blog

# Create the SQLite tables and run the development server
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py runserver 8000

sections.title: Models
sections.description: Map database tables to Python classes with fields and metadata:

snippets.code:
from django.db import models


class Category(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=80, unique=True)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=80, unique=True)

    class Meta:
        verbose_name_plural = "categories"
        ordering = ["name"]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class Tag(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=40, unique=True)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=40, unique=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class Article(models.Model):
    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        DRAFT = "draft", "Draft"
        PUBLISHED = "published", "Published"

    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=200, unique=True)
    body = models.TextField()
    status = models.CharField(max_length=10, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.DRAFT)
    category = models.ForeignKey(Category, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="articles")
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, related_name="articles", blank=True)
    views = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
    published_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["-published_at", "-created_at"]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=["status", "published_at"])]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

sections.title: Migrations
sections.description: Generate, inspect and apply schema changes:

snippets.code:
# Create migration files from model changes
python manage.py makemigrations blog

# Show the SQL a migration will run
python manage.py sqlmigrate blog 0001

# Apply pending migrations
python manage.py migrate

# List applied and pending migrations for one app
python manage.py showmigrations blog

# Create an empty migration for manual operations
python manage.py makemigrations blog --empty --name add_indexes

# Roll back to a previous migration
python manage.py migrate blog 0002

# Collapse several migrations into one file
python manage.py squashmigrations blog 0001 0004

sections.title: URLs
sections.description: Route paths to views and build URLs by name:

snippets.code:
# blog/urls.py
from django.urls import path

from . import views

app_name = "blog"

urlpatterns = [
    path("", views.article_list, name="list"),
    path("2024/archive/", views.article_archive, name="archive"),
    path("<slug:slug>/", views.article_detail, name="detail"),
]

# config/urls.py
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import include, path

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),
    path("blog/", include("blog.urls")),
]

from django.urls import reverse

# Namespaced URL with a keyword argument
reverse("blog:detail", kwargs={"slug": "first-post"})  # "/blog/first-post/"

# Positional arguments work for unnamed patterns
reverse("blog:archive")  # "/blog/2024/archive/"

sections.title: QuerySet
sections.description: Query the database with filters, annotations and bulk operations:

snippets.code:
from django.db.models import Avg, Count, F, Q, Sum

from .models import Article, Category

# Chained filters and slicing
published = Article.objects.filter(status="published", published_at__year=2024)
recent = Article.objects.order_by("-published_at")[:5]

# OR and NOT conditions
featured = Article.objects.filter(Q(status="published") | Q(category__name="News"))
hidden = Article.objects.exclude(status="draft")

# Update with a field reference
Article.objects.filter(status="draft").update(views=F("views") + 1)

# One row per category with aggregates
stats = Category.objects.annotate(
    article_count=Count("articles"),
    avg_views=Avg("articles__views"),
)

# Fetch or create in one call
category = Category.objects.get(slug="news")
article, created = Article.objects.get_or_create(
    slug="hello-world",
    defaults={"title": "Hello World", "body": "First post", "category": category},
)

from django.db.models import Sum

from .models import Article, Author, Book

# Join related rows up front
books = Book.objects.select_related("author").all()
authors = Author.objects.prefetch_related("books").all()

# Insert many rows with one query
Article.objects.bulk_create([
    Article(title="First", slug="first", body="Body one"),
    Article(title="Second", slug="second", body="Body two"),
])

# Aggregate the whole queryset
total = Article.objects.aggregate(total_views=Sum("views"))

sections.title: Middleware
sections.description: Wrap every request and response with a callable component:

snippets.code:
import logging
import time

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class RequestTimingMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        response = self.get_response(request)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
        logger.info("%s %s took %.3f s", request.method, request.path, elapsed)
        response["X-Elapsed-Seconds"] = f"{elapsed:.3f}"
        return response

sections.title: Testing
sections.description: Exercise views and models with the built-in test runner:

snippets.code:
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from .models import Article, Category


class ArticleViewTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.category = Category.objects.create(name="News", slug="news")
        cls.article = Article.objects.create(
            title="Django testing",
            slug="django-testing",
            body="Body text",
            status=Article.Status.PUBLISHED,
            category=cls.category,
        )

    def test_list_shows_published_article(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("blog:list"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(response, "Django testing")

    def test_detail_returns_404_for_draft(self):
        self.article.status = Article.Status.DRAFT
        self.article.save()
        response = self.client.get(reverse("blog:detail", kwargs={"slug": "django-testing"}))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

sections.title: Deployment
sections.description: Prepare static files, run production checks and serve with Gunicorn:

snippets.code:
# Fail on insecure or missing production settings
python manage.py check --deploy

# Collect static files and apply migrations
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput
python manage.py migrate --noinput

# Serve the WSGI application with three workers
gunicorn config.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 3

# Restart the service managed by systemd
sudo systemctl restart blog.service
sudo systemctl status blog.service

# gunicorn.conf.py
bind = "127.0.0.1:8000"
workers = 3
timeout = 30
accesslog = "-"
errorlog = "-"
raw_env = ["DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.production"]

# config/settings/production.py
SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000
SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS = True
SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD = True
X_FRAME_OPTIONS = "DENY"
